section_summaries.individual_presentation: 43-year-old female with a 3-year history of SPS low back pain and gait disturbances associated with SPS numbness and tingling in lower and upper extremities, neck and low back pain, fatigue, muscle stiffness increasing gradually until night, increased difficulty in walking, increased muscle spasms, recurrent falls affecting daily activities, stiffness, pain, balance disorder, and functional limitations
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: diagnosis had been confirmed by a neurologist at a major state hospital high serum level of GAD antibodies confirmed that she has SPS; blood tests, X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scan were done diagnosed as Parkinson’s Disease (PD) initially; high serum level of GAD antibodies confirmed that she has SPS; blood tests, X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scan performed
section_summaries.individual_treatment: physiotherapy and rehabilitation; Pilates training for 1 year, 3 sessions per week with a personal trainer medications at the time of evaluation include gabapentin, benzodiazepine and weekly intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) CP training focusing on strengthening deep postural muscles of the spine providing trunk stabilization
section_summaries.individual_outcome: stopped physiotherapy and rehabilitation treatment due to no improvement in mobility and loss of motivation Range of motion (ROM) values of the patient’s back extension, all movements of the hip, knee flexion–extension, ankle dorsiplantar flexion, all movements of the shoulder and elbow flexion–extension were evaluated Flexibility was measured with the method suggested by Karaduman. Trunk hyperextension, trunk lateral flexion, hip abduction movement flexibility and hamstring and quadriceps femoris muscle flexibility were measured
section_summaries.individual_limitations: No changes were made in the drugs recommended by the neurologist during the study The case has been evaluated in detail at the beginning and end of the study by the primary investigator (BBK) No explicit diagnostic, treatment, or outcome details provided in the snippet
